So the proper fix is to make `stop_watchers` work with the `tw` we have. Since `tw` is not in `@tails`, we need to detach it directly. Let me look at the actual upstream fix.

The actual upstream fix (fluentd PR #3340) was:

```ruby
def stop_watchers(targets_info, immediate: false, unwatched: false, remove_watcher: true)
  targets_info.each_value { |target_info|
    if remove_watcher
      tw = @tails.delete(target_info)
    else
      tw = @tails[target_info]
    end
    if tw
      tw.unwatched = unwatched
      if immediate
        detach_watcher(tw, target_info.ino, false)
      else
        detach_watcher_after_rotate_wait(tw, target_info.ino)
      end
    end
  }
end
```

And the call site was changed to pass a hash. But again, `tw` isn't in `@tails`.
